target_customer: Spanish and Portuguese speaking learners and employers paying for tech and professional training
problem: Quality tech education was mostly in English and unaffordable or unavailable to Latin American learners.

founders.name: Freddy Vega
previous_startups: Earlier company serving Flash programmers, merged with Van Der Henst's to start the business (EdSurge)
founders.background_notes: From Colombia; EdSurge says age 33 in June 2019.

founders.name: Christian Van Der Henst
founders.background_notes: From Guatemala; later reported leaving day to day operations.

technical_complexity.rationale: Video course platform with subscriptions; the hard part was content production, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Spanish language content library and a large community built over years; platform itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows global MOOC platforms acting on Spanish tech training; Platzi stayed independent and acquired Leap technology.

market_need_then: TNW March 2015 reported about 80,000 students, 15,000 paying students, a 70 percent completion rate and about 2.7 million dollars in bootstrapped revenue.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from Mejorando.la to reflect global ambitions, per The Next Web

identity.voice_and_tone: Learning focus, tagline Aprende 20 minutos al dia

branding.brand_signature: Platzi CONF annual event in Colombia and Mexico

rebrands.why: Reflect global ambitions (The Next Web); sources differ on year

branding.community_and_virality: Annual Platzi CONF and a student community; Spanish language sponsorship of a football club reported by Forbes Colombia (unopened).

brand_strength.rationale: Strong regional recognition in Spanish speaking tech education with 7 million students claimed, but evidence on brand as a growth driver is limited.

pivots.to: Company knowledge training with simulated work scenarios (Platzi Business)
pivots.why: Described on YC page; no sourced reason

outcome_analysis: Platzi was profitable and bootstrapped before YC, raised a small seed in 2016, a 6 million Series A in 2019 and a 60 million Series B led by Prosus in 2021, and claims about 7 million students. Its Spanish language focus on an underserved market and strong completion rates drove growth, and it remains independent.
notes: EdSurge 2016 seed page returned 404 on fetch; seed details come from a search snippet of that article. Series B reported as 60M by Prosus and 62M by TechCrunch. Total funding of 205M on one aggregator is unverified. Founding year 2013 to 2014 by source. TNW says YC was its first outside funding. No competitor named in dated sources, so list empty. Platzi acquired Leap technology (date not found).
